title: Calendula-infused oil
subtitle: A golden carrier oil base for balms, face oils, and baby preparations
excerpt: Calendula-infused oil is a carrier oil steeped with dried calendula petals until the oil turns golden-orange and the flower's properties transfer into the oil. It makes a gentle base for face oils, balms, and baby skincare preparations, and can replace plain sunflower oil in any natural cosmetic recipe. One batch infuses 250 ml of sunflower oil over four to six weeks in a warm place, or overnight in a slow cooker on the lowest setting.
sourceNotes: Calendula (Calendula officinalis) oil infusion as a cosmetic base: The Handmade Apothecary by Kim Walker and Vicky Chown (2017). Cold infusion method: 4 to 6 weeks in warm sunlight or a warm place, as documented in The Herbal Apothecary by JJ Pursell (2015). Folk infusion method adapted for the slow cooker: A Modern Herbal by Maud Grieve (1931) cold-infusion principle applied with low heat. Sunflower oil chosen as the carrier for its neutral scent, light texture, and high oleic acid content which mirrors skin lipids.

recipe.batchNotes: The slow-cooker method produces a comparable result to the cold-infusion method in one day rather than six weeks. Use whichever suits the timeline.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cold infusion: fill a jar with dried petals, cover with oil, and leave in a warm, sunny windowsill for four to six weeks, shaking daily. Strain well before use.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: One year in a sealed dark glass bottle at room temperature. Sunflower oil is moderately shelf-stable; the infused oil keeps the same as the base oil. Discard if the oil smells rancid or the colour turns muddy brown.

glossaryTerms.definition: A plant-derived oil used as the base of a cosmetic blend, applied directly to skin or hair. Calendula-infused sunflower oil is a carrier oil, the infusion transfers the flower's character into the oil base.

items.prepNote: plain, light-coloured sunflower oil; the neutral scent lets the calendula come through
dried whole or petals only; must be fully dry, any moisture causes the infusion to go mouldy

content.text: Fill a clean glass jar with the dried calendula. Pour the sunflower oil over the flowers, making sure they are fully submerged. Seal the jar. Leave in a warm, sunny windowsill or a warm room for four to six weeks, shaking daily. The oil will turn increasingly golden-orange as it infuses. When the colour is rich and the oil smells of calendula, strain through muslin into a clean dark glass bottle. Squeeze the petals well to recover the oil. Discard the spent petals.

Place the dried calendula and sunflower oil in the slow cooker. Set to the lowest heat setting (often labelled 'Warm'). The oil should be warm to the touch but should not simmer. Infuse for eight hours, then strain through muslin while still warm.

Use calendula-infused oil in place of plain sunflower oil in any balm, face oil, or body oil recipe. A 100% calendula oil can be used as a standalone face oil, applied to clean skin at night. It absorbs slowly and suits dry or mature skin particularly well.
One year in a sealed, dark glass bottle at room temperature. Discard if the oil smells rancid or the colour turns from golden-orange to muddy brown.
